text:
priya: Quick sync — I'm changing how we annotate responses with routing-tier + quota hints. Want to decide what is safe to surface to customers vs what stays in the console. Low-risk ops but needs consistent UX across SDKs.

tom: Can you paste an example of the new header/field? :thinking:

priya: Sure — thinking a compact envelope that is machine-first and a short human-friendly hint for clients. Example: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Route-Tier: reserved
X-Redwood-Quota-Reason: tenant_quota_exhausted
X-Redwood-Quota-Window: 2026-03-21T12:00Z/2026-03-21T13:00Z
X-Redwood-Client-Hint: quota exceeded — retry after window expires
```

priya: Note: the `X-Redwood-Client-Hint` is optional for clients that want a short string to show end-users. The other X- headers are intended for SDKs/console and telemetry.

liam: Are we keeping numeric subcodes in the body? SDKs rely on them to decide retry/backoff. If we change header semantics we must keep the subcode contract.

priya: Yes — we keep the 429 + subcode in JSON body as the canonical programmatic signal. Headers are supplementary. Example body shape: `{ \"error\": \"quota_exhausted\", \"code\": \"rate.quota.tenant.limit\", \"retry_after_seconds\": 3600 }`

mike: For rollout: feature-flag the headers on a small canary of customers first. Console should display a new "quota badge" and a link to the tenant runbook when the header is present. We should also add a metric for "client-hint-shown" to know how often user-visible hints are present.

eva: Telemetry question — please include route-tier and quota-reason as tags on traces and metrics. We need to correlate these with P99 latency spikes and model-fallback events. Also: console should show the most recent quota reason and a time window, not just a boolean.

tom: UX question for error copy — we should avoid verbatim internal labels for end-users. `tenant_quota_exhausted` is fine for telemetry, but `Your usage limit was reached for this hour` is the client-facing copy. SDKs should map internal codes -> friendly strings.

liam: Agree. Also we need to distinguish transient throttling (burst) vs terminal quota (hard cap). SDKs should treat burst as retryable with backoff, hard cap as non-retryable until explicit admin action. We can add `quota_type` to the body: `burst|hard`

priya: Good call. So final proposal:
- Keep JSON body: canonical code + quota_type + retry_after_seconds
- Add X- headers: machine tags for routing-tier and raw quota reason, optional short client_hint string for UI
- Console: render a "quota badge" with human copy + link to runbook and historical windows
- Telemetry: emit tags on traces/metrics for route-tier, quota_reason, quota_type

mike: For canary, pick 5 orgs (non-production heavy) and enable headers + console badge. Monitor telemetry for any client-side errors caused by SDKs not ignoring unknown X- headers. If OK after 48h, widen to 25 orgs.

release-bot: deploy/rollout started for feature-flag:quota-header-v1 — canary group A (5 orgs) queued at 2026-03-21T12:01:05Z :rocket:

eva: Also add an alert if we see >1% of requests from canary orgs returning malformed JSON body or if SDKs report parsing exceptions.

priya: Action items: tom to add SDK mapping table, liam to update retry logic, eva to add telemetry tags + alert, mike to coordinate canary list and console badge copy. I'll draft the RFC with examples and link to the runbook.

tom: I'll add the mapping table and a small snippet for Ruby/TS SDKs showing how to surface the friendly message.

liam: I'll file PR for retry-decider with explicit handling for `quota_type: \"burst\"` vs `\"hard\"`.

mike: I'll prepare the canary org list and flag rollout playbook.

priya: Thanks all — syncing next on this after the canary results. :thumbsup:
